A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BD3-LM research. All 28 pages in each version, including Appendices A-D, are readable, and the methods, equations, tables, figures and samples can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling experiments, generation evaluations, noise-schedule ablations and efficiency measurements in Sections 4-6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including benchmark perplexities, generation statistics, ablations and generated samples.

M1.justification: Appendix C.2 revises the stated transformer architecture from 128 to 12 attention heads. This is a limited model-specification correction; the block factorization, objectives, attention masks, training algorithms and samplers remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that models were retrained.

E1.justification: Both versions retain LM1B and OWT training, the same seven zero-shot datasets in Table 5, and the same fixed-length and variable-length generation scenarios. Newly mentioned graph and reasoning work does not introduce evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: The respective comparisons retain the same autoregressive, D3PM, SEDD, MDLM and SSD-LM baselines in Tables 1 and 3-7. Newly cited PARD and Diffusion of Thoughts are discussed as related work, not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 changes the reported shared-transformer setting from 128 to 12 attention heads, without documenting reruns. Splits, preprocessing, training budgets, metrics and sample counts remain unchanged. The newly specified MDLM decoding stride is additional disclosure, not an established protocol change.

E4.justification: The single-token case study, noise-schedule comparisons in Tables 2 and 8, training-efficiency analyses in Section 6.3 and Appendix B.7, and Appendix D sample comparisons are retained without substantive additions or removals.

E5.justification: Variance estimators, NELBO variance reporting and Appendix C.4's single Monte Carlo likelihood estimate with low-discrepancy sampling are unchanged. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Tables 1-8, Figure 2, efficiency measurements and Appendix D sample scores retain their reported results. For example, Table 7 still reports BD3-LM with block size 4 at generative perplexities 25.7 and 23.6 for lengths 1024 and 2048.

T1.justification: Appendix A corrects the preceding-time definition from s(i) = t(i-1)/T to s(i) = (i-1)/T, removing an erroneous extra scaling and matching Section 2.2. The substantive NELBO derivations and proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims about block diffusion, arbitrary-length generation, KV caching, variance-reducing schedules and improved diffusion-model perplexity. Replacing 'block-autoregressive models' with 'block diffusion models' in the contribution list clarifies terminology without changing the contribution.

C2.justification: The interpretation of gradient variance as a contributor to the likelihood gap and the discussion of block-size tradeoffs remain unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning training cost, sequential generation, controllability and task-dependent block size.

D1.justification: v3 discloses 110M parameters for AR, SEDD, MDLM and BD3-LMs, versus 400M for SSD-LM in Table 7. Appendix C.5 newly specifies MDLM's 512-token blockwise decoding stride, and Appendix C.2 revises the attention-head count. These improve configuration documentation.

R1.justification: Section 7 and the references add Ye et al.'s Diffusion of Thoughts and Zhao et al.'s PARD. The new PARD discussion distinguishes BD3-LMs through autoregressive/diffusion interpolation, KV caching and attention within noised blocks. This is a localized expansion of research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 lightly rewrites the training explanation in Section 3.2 and efficiency discussion in Section 6.3, corrects author spelling and punctuation, and changes 'log-likelihood' to 'negative log-likelihood' after Equation 8. The overall section and appendix structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 swaps the first two diffusion snapshots to show progressive unmasking. Table 7's caption gains model-size information, and local reflow moves the end of Appendix C.5 onto page 26. No result tables or figures are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility and comparison transparency through the revised head count, explicit model sizes and MDLM decoding stride. The corrected time definition and diffusion illustration remove localized errors, while the added related-work discussion improves attribution. These are useful, limited gains; the core approach and empirical support remain substantially unchanged.
